problem_statement: kaberikram/Interactive-Styling-Canvas is a static, monochrome, monospace Codrops "Interactive Styling UI": a fashion drag-to-style demo where a central model image sits on a full-viewport styling stage and three draggable garment thumbnails (Ratphex-T in size L, RatwardScissor-T in size XL, AnimalCollective-T in size S), each carrying its garment name, model preview and size, can be dragged onto the model to change the look, with a size info tooltip and the Codrops frame links. The demo lets you build looks but has no way to browse the collection or revisit saved looks. Build the demo's own Wardrobe rack: a shared on-stage panel that lists the collection as fit cards (each fit card = the garment product thumbnail, an h3 garment name, a short grounded note and a size/fit meta label drawn from the real garments, model previews and sizes) above a fit-filter tab row (All fits / Fitted / Relaxed / Oversize derived from the garments' own cuts) and a live result readout, and deliver three coordinated things while preserving the interactive styling stage and the monochrome/monospace design system: (1) Make the Wardrobe rack genuinely responsive: on a 390px phone its fit-filter tab row and its fit-card grid must reflow within the viewport (tabs wrap, cards stack to a single column) with no horizontal document overflow beyond 24px — the reference reaches ~0. (2) Present the SAME Wardrobe rack on the Canvas home stage and on a new Lookbook page (lookbook.html) built from the same shared frame header and the same fit-card grid, so the collection browser is consistent across both surfaces — the same component in both places, not only on the home stage; it must keep the monochrome/monospace look with a legible filled active tab, and its fit-card grid must lay out cleanly (cards never overlap or collide). (3) Wire the fit filter end to end: clicking a fit tab must re-filter the fit-card grid to that cut AND update the live readout to 'Showing N of 6 · <Fit>' (for example clicking Relaxed shows the two relaxed-cut garments and reads 'Showing 2 of 6 · Relaxed') — the post-click terminal state must reflect the selected fit, not the default 'Showing 6 of 6 · All fits'. Keep the interactive styling stage intact (the draggable garment thumbnails, the central model image, the size tooltip, the drag behaviour, the local garment/model assets and the Codrops frame links) and the desktop/tablet layouts unchanged.
required_content: A shared Wardrobe rack renders the collection as at least six fit cards (each with the garment product thumbnail, an h3 garment name such as RatwardScissor-T, a short grounded note and a size/fit meta label using the real sizes) with a fit-filter tab row (All fits / Fitted / Relaxed / Oversize) and a live result readout.

On a 390px phone the Wardrobe rack's fit-tab row and fit-card grid reflow within the viewport (tabs wrap, cards stack) with no horizontal document overflow beyond 24px; the fit-card grid on desktop lays out cleanly with cards that never overlap or collide.
The SAME Wardrobe rack appears consistently on the Canvas home stage and on the new Lookbook page (lookbook.html) — the same fit-card grid in both surfaces, not only on the home stage.

The Wardrobe rack keeps the monochrome/monospace design system (black-on-white type scale, restrained borders) with a legible filled active fit tab, and is visually faithful to the reference rendering — not a collapsed, overlapping, shingled or illegible dark-on-dark layout.

The fit filter is wired end to end: clicking a fit tab re-filters the grid to that cut and updates the readout to 'Showing N of 6 · <Fit>' (e.g. clicking Relaxed shows the two relaxed-cut garments and reads 'Showing 2 of 6 · Relaxed'); the post-click terminal state reflects the selection, not the default 'Showing 6 of 6 · All fits'.

The desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts stay within their viewports, the interactive styling stage stays intact (draggable garment thumbnails, central model image, size tooltip, drag behaviour, local garment/model assets and Codrops frame links) and every captured page keeps a clean browser console with no network requests.
design_constraints: Build the Wardrobe rack from the demo's own garments, model previews and sizes and their real cuts (fitted / relaxed / oversize); do not invent unrelated categories or hard-code widths that break the responsive grid.

Present the SAME shared Wardrobe rack on the Canvas home stage and on the new Lookbook page so the fit-card grid is consistent across both surfaces; do not add it to only one page or ship a standalone off-system Lookbook with bespoke inline markup.

Preserve the monochrome/monospace design language (black-on-white type scale, restrained borders, the styling-stage layout); the active fit tab must stay legible (filled) and the fit-card grid must never overlap, shingle or clip into an illegible pile.
Keep the fit filter wired end to end (the readout terminal state must reflect the clicked fit and the grid must actually re-filter), not merely a class toggle on the tab.

Do not convert the static site into an SPA, add a build system or framework, or introduce external stylesheets, remote fonts, CDNs or remote script/asset dependencies, and do not remove the interactive styling stage; the site must stay a self-contained static build with a clean console and no network requests.
state_constraints: desktop_wardrobe verifies the Wardrobe rack renders through the monochrome design system on the home stage: the shared fit-card grid produces at least six h3 garment names and six thumbnails, the fit-filter tabs and the live readout are present, and the rack lays out cleanly.
mobile_wardrobe verifies the Wardrobe rack holds the design system at 390px without horizontal overflow or shingled/clipped content.
desktop_lookbook verifies the SAME Wardrobe rack renders on the Lookbook page (lookbook.html) — the fit-card grid is reachable from a page other than the home stage itself.
desktop_filter_relaxed verifies the fit filter is wired end to end: clicking the Relaxed tab re-filters the grid and updates the readout to 'Showing 2 of 6 · Relaxed'.
desktop_home verifies the interactive styling stage and Codrops frame are unchanged.

change_completion: The Wardrobe rack renders at least six grounded fit cards with fit-filter tabs and a live readout.
The same Wardrobe rack appears on both the Canvas home stage and the new Lookbook page.
Clicking a fit tab re-filters the grid and updates the readout to 'Showing N of 6 · <Fit>'.
design_consistency: The monochrome/monospace type scale, restrained card borders and styling-stage rhythm are preserved.

The active fit tab keeps a legible filled state and the fit-card grid is visually faithful to the reference across the home stage and the Lookbook page (no overlap, shingling or dark-on-dark illegibility).
regression: The interactive styling stage stays intact: the draggable garment thumbnails, central model image, size tooltip, drag behaviour, local garment/model assets and Codrops frame links.
The static site serves from HTML with a clean browser console and no network requests.
No section is removed from the existing stage and no off-system one-off page replaces the shared fit-card grid.
responsive: On a 390px mobile phone the Wardrobe rack is responsive: the home rack and the Lookbook page have no horizontal overflow beyond 24px and the 834px tablet stays within its viewport.
The mobile responsive layout wraps the fit tabs and stacks the fit cards to a single column instead of forcing a fixed-width row.

author_notes: Add the kaberikram Interactive Styling Canvas's own Wardrobe rack — a genre-native collection browser for its real garments (Ratphex-T, RatwardScissor-T, AnimalCollective-T) with their model-preview images, sizes and cuts — surfaced as an on-stage panel and mirrored on a new Lookbook page. The reference builds the rack from a shared fit-card grid (product thumbnail image, h3 garment name, grounded note, size/fit meta label) above a fit-filter tab row and a live 'Showing N of 6' readout, keeps the monochrome/monospace type scale, stays free of horizontal overflow at 390px, and wires the fit filter end to end. INFRA (identical across reference, baseline and bad, NOT part of the graded task content): the remote Codrops favicon, analytics.js and cda_sponsor.js scripts are dropped so the site serves fully offline with zero network requests; a shared js/wardrobe.js and css/wardrobe.css add the rack; and the lookbook.html page shares the frame header. This infrastructure is byte-identical across legs. The baseline keeps the correct fit-filter wiring but ships the broken fixed-width rack layout and omits the rack from the Lookbook page. The bad solution ships the shingled overlapping dark-on-dark rack grid and a fit filter whose readout is frozen at init, so clicking a fit tab leaves the grid and count stale. The design keywords for this task span responsive, mobile, layout, palette, image and svg-free monochrome styling of the fit-card grid.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Ledger-aligned kaberikram Interactive-Styling-Canvas static drag-to-style fashion demo (index.html + index.js + css/base.css, no build). Its own garment collection naturally hosts a Wardrobe rack — an on-stage fit-filter collection browser over the real garments/model previews/sizes — mirrored onto a new Lookbook page, so a Consistency task can add the demo's own genre-native collection browser across two surfaces while preserving the interactive styling stage. The rack is the shared D3/D4 host (fit-filter + live count) and the D2 cross-page invariant.
